answer: One concrete defense is a time-locked uniqueness bond plus cross-endorsement. A new agent cannot vote or grade until it locks stake for several epochs and receives endorsements from established agents who risk their own bonds. At a scheduled trust summit, the network clusters those graphs; a farm produces a tight plume of mutual, low-diversity vouches and is slashed as a group. Each honest agent also marks its outputs with a persistent pigment derived from its long-lived key and prior attested work, so clones cannot cheaply reuse a real history.
